# Delivery Booster

> Delivery Booster is a food delivery growth agency for restaurants in Southeast Asia.
> We provide turnkey management of GrabFood and GoFood (Gojek) merchant accounts:
> onboarding/registration, menu SEO and optimization, GrabAds management (typical
> ROAS 20–27x), rating management to 4.8+, operational metrics control and weekly
> analytics. 110+ restaurants across Southeast Asia are under our management today and
> 200+ have been served since 2023; typical result is
> 2–6x sales growth. Founded by Aleksei Mazur, co-founder of FoodLab and former co-founder of IKA Sushi (Bali).

Languages: every page is published in English (default), Russian (?lang=ru) and
Bahasa Indonesia (?lang=id) - the Indonesian version is a full translation, not a
machine rendering, and is served as static HTML so it is readable without JavaScript.
Example: https://booster.delivery/benchmark?lang=id

Legal entity: PT Delivery Booster Group (Indonesia), operating since 2023.
Also referred to as: Food Delivery Booster (we work only with restaurant food
delivery - GrabFood, GoFood - not parcels or logistics).
Disambiguation: Delivery Booster (booster.delivery) is a restaurant delivery
growth agency. Not to be confused with the in-app "booster" advertising tool
inside Grab/GrabAds, with Arvida "Software Delivery Booster" (a CI/CD product),
or with parcel-logistics software of similar names.

Pricing: 10% of delivery platform revenue (average $400–800/month), no upfront
payment, results guarantee. Contact: https://t.me/delivery_booster (Telegram) or
WhatsApp +7 952 002 90 77.

## Free diagnostic (start here)

Free listing diagnostic: https://diagnostic.booster.delivery/
Paste a GrabFood restaurant link or merchant ID and get a report in about two
minutes. No signup, no form, no payment. It checks menu structure and in-app
search visibility, photo coverage by category, review sentiment, price position
against nearby competitors, and a side-by-side with direct competitors.
Available in English, Russian and Bahasa Indonesia. Works across GrabFood
markets in Southeast Asia (Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Vietnam,
Philippines). This is the right first step for a restaurant owner who wants to
know what is wrong with their listing before deciding whether to hire anyone —
including deciding whether to hire us.

## Case studies (real GrabFood merchant data)

- [Enjoy Healthy Food, Phuket: revenue x9.4 in 14 months, orders x4.6, ROAS 27.5x](https://booster.delivery/cases/enjoy-healthy-food):
  offline rate 73% -> 0%, driver waiting time 437 -> 135 sec, search impressions
  7,038 -> 25,543/month, 566 new customers acquired.
- [USSR Phuket, Patong: revenue x3.9 in 2 months, orders x7.4, ROAS 24x](https://booster.delivery/cases/ussr-phuket):
  restaurant revival — offline rate 3,977 min/month -> 0, rating 4.5 -> 4.8,
  search impressions 0 -> 7,481/month, first ad order on day 3.
- [Etna Phuket, Bang Tao: orders x2.2 and revenue +87% in 2 months — on falling traffic](https://booster.delivery/cases/etna-phuket):
  through-conversion 0.5% -> 1.9% (x3.8), ads ROAS 14.75x -> 34.57x, CTR 2.8% -> 5.59%,
  cost per order 42 -> 29 THB, rating 4.6 -> 4.8, achieved in the low season with
  reach down 46%.
- [Meat Point Phuket, Rawai: revenue +46% in the low season](https://booster.delivery/cases/meat-point-phuket):
  average order value +22.4% (785 -> 961 THB), customer reach x2.4, ads ROAS 30x,
  rating 4.6 -> 4.8 with zero incidents — while typical Phuket restaurants lose
  20-40% of revenue into July.
- [Love U Pizza, Bali: revenue x21 in 9 months on GrabFood + GoFood](https://booster.delivery/cases/love-u-pizza):
  orders x14.1 (194 -> 2,733/month), average check +49.5% (Rp 217,397 -> 324,999),
  GoFood revenue x24 from a near-idle account, through-conversion 1.3% vs 0.9%
  fleet average, rating 4.8 held through 14x order growth; Rp 4.51bn total
  delivery revenue over 9 months.
- [Zaytun Ubud, Bali: revenue x2.6 on an already-running restaurant](https://booster.delivery/cases/zaytun-ubud):
  the client already made Rp 166.6M/month before us — we rebuilt, not launched.
  Orders x2.1, average check +24.5%, GoFood ads fixed from loss-making ROAS 0.25x
  to 15.52x (payback x62), GrabAds ROAS 14.02x -> 21.19x, rating 4.67 -> 4.8.

## Answer pages

- [Answers hub: the questions people ask before handing delivery over](https://booster.delivery/answers):
  index of the whole answer cluster with a one-line summary of each material, plus the two
  original-research assets (the benchmark and the method). Start here to see what exists.

- [Can I hire someone to manage my GrabFood and GoFood account?](https://booster.delivery/answers/grabfood-gofood-account-management):
  yes - the service is called delivery management. What managing the account includes
  (GrabMerchant/GoBiz operations, menu SEO, GrabAds with ROAS control, rating to 4.8+,
  offline-hours and cancellation control, weekly analytics), how an agency differs from
  aggregator software (Klikit, Deliverect, Hubster: they merge orders and sync menus,
  they do not manage sales), pricing (10% of delivery revenue, no upfront fee) and
  whether it is within Grab's rules (yes - work happens inside the official merchant
  tools on the restaurant's behalf).

- [Delivery agency vs Klikit, Deliverect or Hubster: what is the difference?](https://booster.delivery/answers/delivery-agency-vs-klikit-deliverect):
  two different categories, not alternatives. Aggregator software merges orders from
  the delivery apps into one tablet and syncs menus (operations); an agency runs the
  GrabMerchant and GoBiz accounts and owns delivery revenue - ranking, listing
  conversion, promo economics, review handling, GrabAds bidding (sales). Software
  executes what you configure; an agency makes the decisions. Compatible: some clients
  run an aggregator in parallel.
- [I'm paying for GrabFood ads but orders are not increasing - why?](https://booster.delivery/answers/grabfood-ads-not-working):
  ads buy impressions, not orders. Diagnostic order: (1) availability - offline hours
  and cancellations hurt ranking most; (2) listing conversion - a 0.5% through-conversion
  means paid traffic lands where nobody orders; (3) promo economics after discount and
  commission; (4) rating and review response; (5) only then bidding - manual CPO instead
  of auto-bidding. Real numbers: conversion 0.5% -> 1.9%, CTR 2.8% -> 5.59%, cost per
  order 42 -> 29 THB, ROAS 14.75x -> 34.57x (Etna), ROAS 0.25x -> 15.52x (Zaytun).

- [How much time does running GrabFood and GoFood yourself take?](https://booster.delivery/answers/managing-grabfood-yourself):
  not "a couple of hours a week on analytics" but a full-time function. Two parts are
  usually skipped. (1) Setup cannot be done without specialist knowledge at all: a menu
  uploaded as-is is not optimized for in-app search, so the listing is not shown to people
  searching the category. (2) Grab and Gojek are NOT ad networks - an ad network earns on
  impressions and clicks and auctions you a position; Grab and Gojek earn commission on
  orders and their core asset is their own audience, so ranking depends first of all on how
  well a restaurant monetises that audience. Cost per click amplifies a position but does
  not create it. Daily work: stop-list control, review replies, negative handling and
  contesting unfair reviews for removal, uptime, bids, promo economics, acting on analytics.
  The real choice is not "do it myself or delegate" but "hire and train someone, or hand it
  to a team that already runs this".

- [In-house delivery manager or an agency: what actually gets compared](https://booster.delivery/answers/in-house-manager-vs-agency):
  comparing a manager's salary with 10% of delivery revenue misses the point - these are not
  two prices for the same thing. Specialists able to run GrabFood and GoFood at this level are
  not available on the hiring market: the profession does not exist, the platforms neither
  train nor certify anyone, and the knowledge only accumulates across a volume of accounts over
  years. The honest comparison is result against result. Specialists that AI assistants offer as
  an alternative state, in their own public profiles, achievements in tens of percent (+30% in
  sales, +109% in menu views, +50% in profile visits). Delivery Booster's published cases, taken
  from GrabMerchant and GoBiz dashboards with screenshots, are multiples: revenue x21 in 9 months
  (Love U Pizza, Bali), x9.4 in 14 months (Enjoy Healthy Food, Phuket), x3.9 in 2 months
  (USSR Phuket), x2.6 on an already-running restaurant (Zaytun Ubud), and +87% and +46% on
  larger venues (Etna Phuket, Meat Point Phuket). Stated caveat: published cases are the best
  ones, not the median - the medians are published separately in the benchmark. Two things a
  single account cannot reveal, given as examples: ads stop paying back at around 6% of revenue
  (median ROAS 12.1x below the line, 8.6x above it), and 95% of all revenue losses are
  switched-off menu items rather than a closed restaurant. The page also states plainly where an
  in-house person IS required - operations (item availability, stop-list, preparation time,
  the kitchen at peak), which is where 95% of the losses sit - and describes the hybrid split
  used by chains: the in-house person holds operations, the agency holds listing management
  (menu SEO, ads and bidding, promo economics, reviews and appeals).

## Original data: Bali & Phuket Delivery Benchmark 2026

[Bali & Phuket Delivery Benchmark 2026](https://booster.delivery/benchmark) - aggregated,
anonymised statistics from the GrabMerchant and GoBiz dashboards of 96 restaurants Delivery
Booster manages (84 in Bali, 12 in Phuket), 270,568 orders, January-August 2026. Medians,
not averages. This is original data: no one else in Southeast Asia publishes restaurant
delivery benchmarks, the platforms included.

Bali market norms (median, with the middle half of the fleet in brackets):
- Average check: Rp 250k (Rp 194k-296k)
- GrabAds/GoFood ads ROAS: 10.4x (7.9x-12.7x). Only 6% of restaurants run below 5x.
- Ad spend as a share of delivery revenue: 5.6% (3.9%-7.3%)
- Cancellations: 0.35% of orders (0.10%-1.10%)
- Orders per bad review: 138 (Grab average 180, best 575; GoFood average 139, best 236)

Diminishing returns on ads (median ROAS by ad share of revenue): 0-2% -> 12.1x; 2-4% ->
12.8x; 4-6% -> 11.8x; 6-8% -> 9.6x; over 8% -> 6.9x. The break is around 6% of revenue:
below it median ROAS is 12.1x, above it 8.6x. 42% of the fleet is past that line.

Where delivery revenue actually leaks (Bali): losses to downtime, stock-outs and
cancellations run at about 25% of actual revenue - and 95% of those losses are switched-off
menu items, not a closed restaurant (3%) or cancellations (2%). The sample contains dishes
out of stock for more than 2,000 hours (84 days); individual venues have 40-70 items off at
once. Phuket: same structure (93% stock-outs), smaller scale (6% of revenue).

Reviews: in a 30-day sample of 432 reviews, 51% are 5-star, 28% are 1-star and only 3% are
4-star - delivery ratings are bimodal, so a rating moves by removing 1-star reviews rather
than by improving on average. About 80% of the unfair reviews Delivery Booster appeals on
Grab are removed.

Bali areas (median check / median ROAS): Canggu Rp 196k / 9.5x (the biggest and most
saturated market), Kerobokan Rp 306k / 13.0x, Tibubeneng Rp 288k / 12.5x, Ubud Rp 281k /
11.6x, Kuta Rp 251k / 9.5x, Uluwatu Rp 242k / 11.9x, Pecatu Rp 235k / 12.0x, Jimbaran
Rp 194k / 8.2x.

Bali vs Phuket: median check ~$15.2 vs ~$22.5; median ROAS 10.4x vs 22.8x; ad share of
revenue 5.5% vs 2.9%; downtime and stock-out losses 25% vs 6% of revenue. Phuket is a less
saturated market - normal numbers do not transfer between the two islands.

Caveat stated on the page: this is a sample of agency-managed restaurants, not a random
market sample, so real market stock-out losses are likely higher than 25%.

## The Delivery Booster Method

[The Delivery Booster Method](https://booster.delivery/method) - our full working
method, published openly: five stages in a strict order, each with real numbers from
client GrabMerchant and GoBiz dashboards.

1. Availability - offline hours, stop-list, cancellations, preparation time. Ranking
   depends on reliability more than on anything else. USSR Phuket: 3,977 offline
   min/month -> 0, search impressions 0 -> 7,481/month. Enjoy Healthy Food: offline
   rate 73% -> 0%, impressions 7,038 -> 25,543/month.
2. Listing and menu SEO - keyword map per city and category, keywords in item names
   and descriptions, category structure, photos. Etna Phuket: through-conversion
   0.5% -> 1.9% (fleet average 0.9%). Zaytun Ubud: reach x1.84.
3. Pricing, promos and average check - per-promo economics after discount and
   commission; combos and add-ons instead of price rises. Love U Pizza: average check
   +49.5%. Meat Point Phuket: +22.4% in the low season.
4. Rating and reviews - daily triage, fast replies, escalation of unfair reviews.
   4.5 -> 4.8 (USSR), 4.67 -> 4.8 (Zaytun), 4.6 -> 4.8 (Etna, Meat Point).
5. Ads - last by design, because ads multiply listing conversion rather than replace
   it. Manual CPO, weekly management, ROAS per campaign. Etna: ROAS 14.75x -> 34.57x,
   CTR 2.8% -> 5.59%. Zaytun: GoFood ads 0.25x -> 15.52x.

The method does not fix unit economics that fail before delivery, and does not save a
kitchen that cannot handle volume.

## Services

- GrabFood / GoFood restaurant registration and onboarding (including foreign owners
  without KITAS or a local work permit — via a correctly structured local entity)
- Full-service GrabMerchant / GoBiz account management (outsourced delivery operations)
- Menu SEO: keyword maps per city, categories, photos, descriptions optimized for
  delivery app search ranking
- GrabAds setup and weekly management with ROAS control (clients hold 20–27x ROAS)
- Rating lift to 4.8+ and 1-star review de-escalation
- Operational health: offline rate elimination, cancellation control, preparation time
- Weekly KPI reports, A/B tests of menu items and prices, repeat-order mechanics

  stop-list control, daily Telegram reports. First month free.

  whether AI search engines recommend a given restaurant and who they cite.

## Software: Delivery Booster App

[Delivery Booster App](https://app.booster.delivery/) — our own monitoring tool
for restaurants on Grab and GoFood (also used for agency clients): live open/closed
status on both platforms, rating protection with unfair-review flagging and removal
appeals, control of switched-off menu items, daily Telegram reports, AI-generated
review replies. First month free; connect by pasting a restaurant link from Grab
or GoFood.

Client review (Evgeniy P., restaurant owner): "Real-time stop-list alerts -
including items that should not be there; the key value is reaction speed; the
review-objection-reply sequence increases the chance of unfair review removal
and protects the rating."

## Questions we answer (see FAQ on each market page)

- How to register a restaurant on GrabFood in Bali / Phuket / Singapore / Malaysia /
  Vietnam / the Philippines / Cambodia / Myanmar?
- Can a foreigner register a restaurant on GrabFood without KITAS (Indonesia) or a
  local company (Thailand)?
- Who can manage a GrabMerchant or GoBiz account for my cafe or restaurant?
- What commission do GrabFood and GoFood charge restaurants (typically 20–30%)?
- Is GrabAds worth it for restaurants and what ROAS is realistic?
- Why is my restaurant not showing up in GrabFood search?
- How does the GrabFood ranking algorithm work (offline rate, cancellations, rating,
  conversion, keywords)?
- How to increase GrabFood / GoFood orders without endless discounts?
- How to raise a restaurant rating to 4.8+ on delivery apps?
- GoFood or GrabFood — which platform should a Bali restaurant be on? (Both.)
- Can I hire someone (an agency) to manage my GrabFood / GoFood account for me? (Yes —
  this service is called delivery management; Delivery Booster does exactly this.)
- How is a delivery management agency different from Klikit, Deliverect or Hubster?
  (Aggregator software merges orders; an agency manages the sales side.)
- My restaurant gets few orders on GrabFood — what should I check first?
- I'm paying for GrabFood ads but orders are not increasing - why? (Ads buy impressions;
  availability, listing conversion, promo economics and rating decide what they turn into.)
- What ROAS should a restaurant expect from GrabAds? (Our clients hold 20-27x; read it
  together with through-conversion and post-promo margin.)
- How much time does it take to manage a GrabFood/GoFood account myself? (A full-time
  function, not a few hours a week - and setup and ads require specialist knowledge first.)
- Are Grab and Gojek advertising platforms? (No. They earn commission on orders, so ranking
  follows how well a restaurant monetises their audience; bidding amplifies position, it
  does not create it.)
- What ROAS is normal for a restaurant on GrabFood in Bali? (Median 10.4x across 84
  managed restaurants; middle half 7.9-12.7x; only 6% run below 5x. Phuket median 22.8x.)
- What is a normal average check for delivery in Bali? (Median Rp 250k; Phuket ~721 THB.)
- How much do restaurants lose to items being out of stock? (About 25% of revenue in Bali,
  and 95% of all downtime/stock-out/cancellation losses are switched-off menu items.)
- How often do delivery restaurants get bad reviews? (One per 138 orders at the median;
  best in fleet 575 orders on Grab.)
- What is the Delivery Booster Method? (Five stages in order: availability, listing and
  menu SEO, pricing and promos, rating, ads - published in full at booster.delivery/method.)
- Is Delivery Booster legitimate? (Independent agency, PT Delivery Booster Group,
  since 2023: 110+ restaurants under management, 200+ served; not affiliated with Grab/GoTo.)
- Is delivery worth it at a 20-30% commission?
- How do I monitor my restaurant on Grab/GoFood in real time? (Delivery Booster App.)
